meta.title: Combat Round Resolution
meta.subtitle: One melee swing end to end: swing budget, one attack roll against every affordable defense, three-channel damage

views.label: How many swings you get
views.note: calcSwingCount turns dexterity, weapon speed and skill into a number, then stamina and carried weight scale it down. Cap is 4.

views.label: One attack roll, rolled once
views.note: The swing is rolled a single time. Its score is dexterity plus combat skill, scaled by stamina, position and light. No armor is read.

views.label: One roll per affordable defense
views.note: Every affordable defense is rolled separately against that one attack value, using the attacker's spread. The widest margin wins.

views.label: Two floors that can reverse the verdict
views.note: Two symmetric floors run after the margin, so an outclassed defender can still save and a beaten attacker can still land the swing.

views.label: Damage, then the words for it
views.note: One raw formula serves all three channels. Mitigation is a capped percentage, and the number becomes a phrase before a player sees it.

messages.label: engaged with a target
messages.note: Combat is driven by the world tick, not by a command. Every 4 second round, handleCombatRound runs once per engaged pair.

messages.label: how many swings for this weapon?
1 to 4, after stamina and carried weight
messages.note: calcSwingCount: dexterity, weapon speed and skill set the base, then a stamina multiplier and an over-capacity weight penalty of up to 50 percent scale it down. Hard cap of 4 per weapon.

messages.label: resolve this swing at attack score S
messages.note: calcAttackScore builds S from dexterity, combat skill, a dual-wield penalty, stamina, prone position, darkness and flight. It never reads a mitigation field. Armor changes how much a landed hit hurts, never whether it lands.

messages.label: roll the swing ONCE, spread = StdDevFor(S)
messages.note: runBestOfAllDefense opens with atkStdDev := dice.StdDevFor(atkScore) and attackRoll := dice.Roll(atkScore, atkStdDev). This is the only attack roll in the whole exchange, no matter how many defenses follow.

messages.label: one value A, and the spread that made it
messages.note: Both halves are kept. A is the number every defense must beat, and the attacker's spread becomes the spread every defense rolls with, so the two sides of the contest share one shape of randomness.

messages.label: which defenses do you have?
dodge, parry, block
messages.note: Dodge scores dexterity plus unarmed-combat skill. Parry scores dexterity plus weapon-combat skill plus the best equipped weapon's ParryRating. Block scores the mean of strength and dexterity plus weapon-combat skill plus the best shield's BlockRating. Those ratings are ItemSpec fields entirely separate from physical_mitigation.

messages.label: skipped: cannot pay this one's stamina
messages.note: Each defense has a stamina cost. If the defender's current stamina is below it the loop simply continues, so that defense is never rolled at all. Low stamina never lowers a defense's score. It removes the defense from the contest entirely, which costs the defender far more.

messages.label: roll dodge vs A, attacker's spread
roll parry vs A, attacker's spread
messages.note: Every surviving defense gets its own independent dice.Roll(defenseScore, atkStdDev). They compete with each other over the same attack value rather than each facing a fresh swing, which is what stops a defender with three defenses from getting three separate chances at three different attacks.

messages.label: roll block vs A, attacker's spread
a margin each: defenseRoll - A
messages.note: One number per defense. Positive means that defense beat the swing, negative means it lost and by how much. Position, darkness, rally, grapple and mutation modifiers have already been folded into each defense score before this point.

messages.label: widest margin picks the defense, win or lose; only that defense pays stamina
messages.note: The largest margin is kept even when every margin is negative, so the closest failure is the one that gets narrated. Stamina is deducted once, for the winning defense only, after all the rolls are done.

messages.label: MinDefenseChance: save anyway
messages.note: If the attack won the margin, resolveDefenseOutcome still gives the defender a flat MinDefenseChance roll, default 0.15. An outclassed defender is never a guaranteed target.

messages.label: MinAttackHitChance: land anyway
messages.note: The mirror image. If a defense won the margin, a flat MinAttackHitChance roll can still turn it into a hit. The two floors are symmetric, checked after the margin, and either can overturn the contest.

messages.label: hit, miss, crit or fumble
messages.note: resolveDefenseOutcome orders the result: double fumble first, then fumbles, then crit versus crit, then a one-sided crit, then the normal margin. Each floor sits inside one branch of that last step, so only ever one can fire.

messages.label: stat x skill x weapon x channel scale x global
messages.note: CalcRawDamage is one formula for all three channels: physical uses strength, magical uses willpower, conviction uses charisma. A configured per-channel scale and a global multiplier finish it.

messages.label: subtract mitigation, capped
messages.note: ApplyMitigation reduces raw damage by the defender's summed equipment percentage for that channel, clamped to the channel cap (default 75 percent). This is the only place armor is consulted in the entire round. A critical hit bypasses mitigation entirely: armor does not reduce crit damage at all.

messages.label: roll variance around the mean
damage for this swing
messages.note: dice.RollStat derives its spread from the mean using the global RollSpread knob, so the shape of every roll in the engine moves with one number.

messages.label: turn the number into a phrase
messages.note: GetDamageDescription converts damage to a share of the target's maximum health and returns light wounds, serious wounds, critical injuries and so on.

messages.label: "causing serious wounds"
messages.note: The raw integer never leaves the engine. Attacker, defender and every spectator in the room read the same descriptive band.

cards.title: Swing budget
items: Dexterity, weapon speed and combat skill set the base swing count
Low stamina and carrying too much weight both scale it down
Hard cap of 4 swings per weapon, minimum of 1

cards.title: The opposed roll
items: The attack score is dexterity plus combat skill, with no mitigation term
The swing is rolled once, and its spread is reused by every defense roll
Dodge, parry and block each roll separately and each produce a margin
The widest margin wins, even when every margin is a loss
Only the winning defense pays stamina, and it pays it after the rolls

cards.title: What drops out and what overturns
items: A defense the defender cannot pay for is skipped before it is ever rolled
MinDefenseChance, default 0.15, can save a defender the swing already beat
MinAttackHitChance runs the other way and lands a swing a defense stopped
Weapon ParryRating and shield BlockRating feed defense, not mitigation

cards.title: Damage and text
items: One raw formula serves physical, magical and conviction damage
Mitigation is a percentage with a per-channel cap, default 75 percent
The final number is converted to a phrase before any player sees it
